body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{crit}}\), derive the complete \(s=1\) cutoff/effect-label limit experiments separately on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{slope}}\), where \(\tau_n\to\tau\in(0,\infty)\), and on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{entropy},0}\cup\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{entropy},\lambda}\), where \(\tau_n\to\infty\) and \(\lambda_n\to\lambda\in[0,\infty)\). Include boundary-truncated mixtures and every surviving second-order coordinate. Evaluate the fixed-\(\alpha\) minimax expected connected-interval length as \(\mathcal V_\alpha(\tau,\lambda;1)\), and determine whether causal-valid location mixtures together with same-class slope-kink alternatives are least favorable in the full model. Require only the certified reduction \(\mathcal V_\alpha(0,0;1)=2(1-\alpha)\) at the flat boundary; no exact value is asserted on a finite-positive face before the decision problem is solved.
body.justification: The non-Gaussian decision value, rather than cutoff consistency alone, is the unresolved critical object governing honest interval length.
body.gap: Elliott and M\"uller (2014) solve a parametric moderate-break process problem and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022) give an abstract weak-GMM decision theory; Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) keep the fuzzy-RD cutoff fixed. None derives this binary H\"older moving-cutoff experiment, its signed causal label, or its connected-length value.
body.consumer: The value map tells fuzzy-RD users how much interval informativeness remains at each empirically relevant combination of weak compliance and cutoff uncertainty.

obligation.what_is_open: The complete finite-positive \(s=1\) cutoff/effect-label limit experiments, including boundary-truncated location mixtures, every surviving second-order coordinate, the value \(\mathcal V_\alpha(\tau,\lambda;1)\), and full-model least favorability are not determined by the frozen primitives.
obligation.obstruction: The moving-cutoff continuum supplies pairwise Kullback--Leibler and total-variation comparisons to \(P_0\), but these do not determine the joint likelihood-ratio process, the covariance and drift of the required second-order coordinates, or an upper decision rule attaining a finite-face value over the full class. Population profile separation is a deterministic localization inequality and cannot replace convergence of experiments.
obligation.attempted: I derived the full-label coverage-integral lower bound from the causal continuum and evaluated it explicitly on every finite \(\tau\) face. This closes the flat boundary but does not certify that the continuum or a truncated location mixture is least favorable in the full model.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved continuum gives a nontrivial finite-face lower value, although it does not identify the full limit experiment.  Indeed, retaining the \(|t|\)-dependent total-variation bound in prop:moving-cutoff-membership-kl and repeating the coverage integration from thm:flat-face-exact-value yields, whenever \(\tau_n\to\tau\in[0,\infty)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge G_\alpha(\tau)
 :=2\int_0^1[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau t}]_+\,dt.
\]
Writing \(a=1-\alpha\), direct integration gives the computable formula
\[
 G_\alpha(\tau)=
 \begin{cases}
 2a-\dfrac{16}{3}\sqrt\tau,&0\le\tau\le a^2/16,\\[4pt]
 \dfrac{a^3}{24\tau},&\tau>a^2/16.
 \end{cases}
\]
In particular \(G_\alpha(0)=2(1-\alpha)\), agreeing with the exact flat-boundary value.
